headline: Compliance hearing set for Sahel Restaurant & Lounge, 135 Central Street, over alleged alcohol rule violations.
summary: Police Superintendent Gregory Hudon asked for the hearing over alleged violations of alcoholic beverages regulations on October 29th and 31st, 2026. The matter will be discussed at that hearing on December 3rd, 2026. A public hearing on Showcase Cinema Lowell's license transfer at 31 Reyes Ave was continued to the same date, and a hearing was set for Brothers & Company Sports Bar and Grill at 199 to 203 Cabot Street. A one-day wine and malt license was approved for the Bomb Shelter Comedy Showcase.
decisions: Accepted and placed on file a state lottery notice about a keno license for Lowell Asian Bakery and Restaurant.
Continued the public hearing on the Showcase Cinema Lowell license transfer to December 3rd.
Set a public hearing for December 3rd on an all alcoholic beverages restaurant license for Brothers & Company Sports Bar and Grill.
Scheduled a compliance hearing for December 3rd on misconduct allegations against Sahel Restaurant & Lounge.
Approved a special one-day wine and malt beverage license for the Bomb Shelter Comedy Showcase on November 20th, 2026.
discussion: Comedy show license: The applicant said about 25 to 30 people would attend, and that one bartender with a TIPS certificate would serve.
Sahel compliance hearing: Members asked whether the captain needed to speak, and were told the vote only scheduled the hearing, where the matter would be discussed.
Keno license notice: Members confirmed that the city had taken no action against the restaurant, and police had nothing pending.

decision_evidence.quote: Make a motion to accept and place on file. ... Aye. Aye. ... Opposed? Nobody.
I'll make a motion to continue till December 3rd. ... Moved and seconded. All in favor say, "Aye." Aye. Aye.
Motion to put it off till December 3rd. ... Moved and passed.
Second. ... All in favor say, "Aye." Aye. Aye.
Motion to approve. ... Moved and seconded. All in favor say, "Aye." Aye. Aye. Opposed? You've got your license.
